lora_merge.Why merge a LoRA adapter before serving,: Count the matmuls an unmerged LoRA layer runs per call, then ask what the layer looks like after merging.
lora_merge.Why keep the adapter matrices after merg: Think about serving several adapters on one base model, and about resuming training. What would you need that a deleted A and B cannot give you?
lora_merge.Write the merged weight in terms of W, A: Start from W' = W + (alpha / r) B A. Check the shapes of B and A and confirm the product matches W.
lora_merge.Why must the merge update the weight in: Optimizers, FSDP shards and tied weights hold a reference to the weight Parameter. Consider what each of them sees after you assign a new tensor, and what autograd records without no_grad.
lora_merge.What happens if merge() is called twice,: Trace two merge() calls in a row on the weight. Which piece of state lets the second call tell that it has nothing to do?
lora_merge.Is merge then unmerge exact in bf16? Why: Follow W + d - d through bf16 rounding one step at a time. Then name two ways production stacks keep the round trip safe.
lora_merge.Merged single-adapter serving versus unm: Compare per-token latency, memory, and the number of adapters one deployment can serve. Mention batched LoRA kernels such as S-LoRA or Punica.
lora_merge.Can you merge a LoRA trained on a 4-bit: The adapter was trained against the dequantized base. Think about what requantizing W + delta to 4 bits does to a small delta.

dora.What is DoRA, and how does it differ fro: Split each output row of W into a length and a unit direction. Say which part LoRA updates and which part gets its own parameter.
dora.What do the magnitude vector and the dir: Describe what each part controls for one output unit. Count the extra parameters per layer in terms of out_features.
dora.Along which axis is the weight norm take: The weight is (out x in), and you want one scale per output unit. Pick the axis that gives that.
dora.How must the magnitude be initialized so: Write the output of a fresh layer with B = 0 and ask which value of m makes it equal the base layer.
dora.Why does DoRA detach the norm in backwar: Section 4.3 of the paper treats ||W + delta W|| as a constant. Name the gradient term this drops and what memory it saves.
dora.How do you merge a trained DoRA adapter: Is the adapted layer still one linear map? Write its weight in terms of m, W and delta W.
dora.DoRA versus LoRA at the same rank: accur: Weigh accuracy at the same rank against the per-step cost of rebuilding W' and its norm.
dora.What does DoRA cost when the base model: Ask what the norm needs from the base weight each step when the base is 4-bit. Compare with what QLoRA needs.

prefix_tuning.How does HuggingFace PEFT hand the prefi: Think about how a transformers model accepts cached keys and values from earlier tokens, and what PEFT has to add to the attention mask.
prefix_tuning.Prefix tuning versus LoRA: trainable par: Compare trainable parameters, inference compute and KV-cache cost, and whether each method can be merged away.
prefix_tuning.Why does the original paper reparameteri: Think about optimization stability when the prefix is trained directly. What does the paper put between the parameters and the prefix, and what does it keep after training?
